_comments: Declares Order Headers -> Order Lines as a related-record collection (MJ 6.1).
CodeGen reads RelatedRecordCollection and emits a typed `Lines` accessor onto the GENERATED
entity class, so both tiers get it: the browser can add lines to an order and save the whole
graph in one call, and OrderEntityServer inherits the same collection to run booking against.
That replaces the hand-rolled `_lines` array, the Orders.SaveOrder remote operation and the
client-draft hydration that existed only to carry lines over the wire.
RelatedEntity and RelatedEntityJoinField are deliberately NOT set here — they are already
columns on this same row (Order Lines / OrderHeaderID). Duplicating them would create two
sources of truth with the JSON copy winning silently.
Keyed by entity NAMES rather than the row's ID: EntityRelationship IDs are minted by CodeGen,
so a hardcoded UUID would stop matching the first time this database is rebuilt from zero —
which is routine here, since schema changes edit the baseline migration in place.

_comments: Declares Payment Headers -> Payment Lines as a related-record collection (MJ 6.1).
Same treatment as Order Headers -> Order Lines, and for the same reason: PaymentHeaderEntityServer
held a `_lines` array plus a getter/setter pair that existed only on the server, so a payment and
its allocations could not be composed in the browser.
RelatedEntity and RelatedEntityJoinField (Payment Lines / PaymentHeaderID) are already columns on
this row and are deliberately not duplicated here.
NO Sequence policy, unlike Order Lines. PaymentLine has no line-number column — an allocation is
identified by which order line it pays, not by position — so there is nothing to renumber, and
declaring a sequence against a field that does not exist would fail at save time.
OrderBy AllocatedAt: allocations are read in the order they were made, which is what a remittance
shows.
